packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-15 -- unverified image reading (blind first reader)

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed an identification of the work. The overview shows modern pencil shelf labels on the pieces ("Stams, STA, Frg. 118-1r", "Stams, STA, Frg. 118-2r"); I note them as visible labels only and drew nothing from them.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001, overview, face A)
- Four parchment fragments on black ground, with colour chart, scale and two clear plastic weights.
- Upright orientation; single-column vernacular (German-looking) prose in a cursive bookhand (Bastarda-type), brown ink, no rubrics visible at overview scale, no enlarged initials seen.
- Piece 1 (upper right, largest; label "Frg. 118-1r"): c. 26 lines; left edge shows a strip that is a separate cut edge/fold with small stitching holes; a later hand has written small numbers in the left margin ("27", "37" ...?) beside some lines. Top lines faint/abraded.
- Piece 2 (narrow vertical strip, centre): line-ends only (column right edge?), c. 20 short line fragments; pencil label on it.
- Piece 3 (lower left; label "Frg. 118-2r"): c. 18 lines of main text, plus at its left a narrow strip of line-ends from another column or page (separated by a fold/crease line).
- Piece 4 (lower right strip; label "Frg. 118-1r"): c. 5-6 lines, damaged by holes.
- Tiles: image-002 = narrow strip; image-003/004 = piece 1 (upper / lower halves, overlapping); image-005/006 = piece 3 (upper / lower); image-007 = piece 4.
- Face B overview = image-008 with tiles 009-014 (survey added when viewed).

=== image-002 (narrow strip, face A; pencil label reads "Stams, STA, Frg. 118-3r") ===
Line-ends of a single column; vertical ruling line at right; text right-justified to it. Left part of each line cut away.

002.02  [..]dem er   (two short strokes "=" in right margin, a mark)
002.03  [..]ch(?)en alles
002.04  [..]ueff dem (?)  ("ruef(f)"? first letter lost)
002.05  [..]rimpt (?)  ("nimpt"?)
002.06  [..]l er fület (?)   ("erfület"/"er fullet"?) ; in right margin a marginal "Du"/"Bu"? (later? lighter ink)
002.07  [..]d(?) paue (?)   ; three-dot mark in right margin beside this line
002.08  [..]rmels (?)  ("himels"?)
002.09  [..]lfporn (?) / [..]lfp(?)orn  -- unclear
002.10  [..]n dem
002.11  [..]hennge (?) / [..]chung ge
002.12  [..]ber alles  (prob. "uber alles")
002.13  [..]ayler (?)  ("hayler"? "saylet"?)
002.14  [..]zu d(er) (?) / "zu [ ]sche"(?)  -- abbreviated, uncertain
002.15  [..]auchet (?)
002.16  [..]den (?) dy (?) 
002.17  [..]ff g(?) v(?)n   -- very faint, at foot
Limitations: only 1-3 words per line survive; ink faded; readings tentative.

=== LIMITATIONS / SUMMARY ===
- All 14 images opened (2 overviews, 12 tiles). No crops made. Did not stop on the image limit.
- Script: Upper German cursive (Bastarda-like); abbreviations: d with superscript = der; tilde = n/m/en; "ew" with stroke = ewangelium; "v(er)bu(m)", "ma(n)". Latin quotations sometimes underlined (012.05-06, 012.12, 011.07 "Ascendit").

Narrow strips (002, 009, and the side strips on pieces 3 and 1v) give only 1-3 words per line.

- Column/page order of the side strips relative to the main columns is not determined from these images.
